factual_claims.claim: Differential Privacy Reversal via LLM Feedback allows attackers to re-identify individuals from anonymized datasets by analyzing model confidence scores, logits, and perplexity.
A 2025 study published in the Journal of King Saud University found that LLMs face deep-seated privacy vulnerabilities throughout their lifecycle, from pre-training to deployment.
A 2025 NeurIPS study revealed a power-law relationship between the number of training examples and per-example membership inference vulnerability.
A 2025 Amazon Science study introduced PREMIA, a novel reference-based attack framework for membership inference against preference data.
A 2025 ICLR study introduced canary-based privacy auditing, allowing for the first nontrivial privacy audit of an LLM trained with differential privacy.
A 2026 systematic review of 74 studies found that differential privacy via DP-SGD can maintain clinically acceptable performance under moderate privacy budgets (epsilon <= 10).
Google's VaultGemma (2025) demonstrated that 1B-parameter models can be trained with strong differential privacy guarantees.
